column4: train.sh's move gate (is_move_candidate) made any diff to scripts/checks/root_inventory.txt a legacy/ move needing an accepted acceptance rehearsal, so wip/decisions-followup, which only adds docs/proposals to the inventory, passed check (gates and review) and green CI and was still refused by land. Structural cause: one file carries two obligations, the P7 move rehearsal (top-level entries, legacy/) and the minimal-root inventory (first-level docs/ and scripts/ entries too), and the gate keyed on the file instead of on the move's own facts. Fixed on wip/fix-landing-machinery (c064cc7d): the gate compares the top-level entry set the inventory lists at base and head (comments, order and nested entries ignored); a legacy/ change or a non-tree legacy still triggers; root_inventory.sh is unchanged

column4: Review failed open in the landing path: train.sh check set review=0 when no review command existed (no error), its review leg rejected only a published findings note (absent, malformed or blocked passed after a zero exit), and land read no review record at all, so a check run with --no-review landed like any other (facts-decision landed at ab537833d after train.sh check --no-review). Structural cause: review was enforced only as one leg's exit status inside check, a missing reviewer was mapped to a disabled leg, and land trusted CI alone: no reader of review provenance existed at land time. Fixed on wip/fix-landing-machinery (a173432e): check fails with no review command; review_provenance (verify.sh on origin's notes: a clean head note, or with no head note a clean note on every member at its exact SHA) gates both the review leg and land
column7: check fails without a review command; land refuses a train without review provenance; landing_script.sh controls show absent, malformed, blocked and findings notes, at the head or on a member, cannot qualify; the change is on main

column4: scripts/land/acceptance.sh's check leg ran train.sh check --no-review --no-remote, so an accepted rehearsal (the record the move gate trusts) could rest on a check that skipped review, and agents cannot run it (the permission system treats --no-review as a CI bypass); both its build leg and its broken-build control defaulted to make build, which the restarted root (no Makefile; nix develop --command lake build) does not have; its header described only --no-review and make build. Structural cause: the rehearsal scripted its own exemption from a required leg and copied the old tree's build entry point into two places, so it drifted when the root changed. Fixed on wip/fix-landing-machinery (9b48910f): check --no-remote with the review leg passing on verified notes; one BUILD_CMD default for both build legs; header corrected; a landing_script.sh structural control

column4: scripts/review/review.sh's prompts (standard and neutral) made any patch touching what an owner decision covers a finding, with no distinction between choosing a side and recording an answer the owner explicitly gave under docs/decisions.md's recording rule; the review leg refused the facts-decision recording batch, which then landed with check --no-review on a separate manual Codex ACCEPT. column4: Sandboxes inherit the caller's git environment. scripts/checks/review_tool.sh isolated git config only, not the repository-locating variables; a pre-push hook of a LINKED worktree exports GIT_DIR=<repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>, so every git -C <sandbox> in the check acted on the caller. On 2026-11-06 `train.sh ci laudit` run from the linked worktree ~agent/audit-records made the hook's review_tool.sh create its test branches (nonff, capped, parse-*) and set core.bare=true in ~agent/audit-clone (kept unchanged as evidence), and push 28 commits to origin refs/notes/concrete-review (tip b4b364f4, pre-leak 5b6add0d) and 12 to refs/notes/concrete-review-findings (tip 21c56796, pre-leak fd3c6451), authored Review Gate, 17:16:49-17:17:43Z, annotating 21 sandbox commits that exist on no remote (first counted as 22, which wrongly included c54679c3, a real commit whose note at 17:21Z is legitimate); no earlier note was deleted or changed and every reader looks notes up by exact SHA, so none can count as provenance for a real commit. lambdaclass has no notes refs. Codex confirmed with a bounded reproducer on concrete-ci-2 at main f9a8c333 (caller refs and refs/notes/* changed: LEAK) and an independent GIT_DIR experiment. landing_script.sh and landing_bot.sh unset only five of git's local variables; legacy_frozen.sh, acceptance.sh, run-at-ref.sh and bot.sh unset none. Second incident, same cause: the first reproducer installed a pre-push hook that ran review_tool.sh; the leaked GIT_DIR made each nested push re-enter that hook, the recursion exhausted fede-256gb (load ~1900) and the OOM killer took down the orchestrator's session. Structural owner: the sandbox helper scripts/checks/lib/git_sandbox.sh (unsets every `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` variable), sourced by every repository-making script; reproducers and tests run with no installed hook, under timeout 120 and a 512-task / 8G systemd scope bound, or a finite cgroup memory.max plus a process limit, and never an unbounded run. Closed 2026-11-07: the fix landed at dbe838488891, where every closure part is checked in Root checks (scripts/checks/run.sh, all 11 pass: sandbox_isolation PASS=13 FAIL=0 with its structural leg over 9 scripts, the two live linked-worktree probes and the leaking control; landing_script PASS=208 FAIL=0 with the linked-worktree, hook-off, foreign-hook and identify refusal legs; also run on concrete-ci-2 at 8e62e377) (train siso from a full clone; reviewed by Codex, rounds clean at 8e62e377, and Kimi; CI run 42424663064; main CI 42425007584 on origin and 42425010605 on lambdaclass, both success). The stray notes were removed from origin by one forward fast-forward commit per ref on its then-current tip, no force: refs/notes/concrete-review d4bdcae22d50 -> dcffeea8e6cd (21 entries removed, 224 untouched at the push; Codex confirmed the list against the earlier tip 8cbb7db253f7, where 223 were untouched, and the one commit between that tip and d4bdcae22d50 only added a legitimate note for 9d6dc01a, so the removal list is identical) and refs/notes/concrete-review-findings 301e929e1bab -> 5d7c6dc3dad5 (11 removed, 105 untouched); the 40 leaked commits wrote 33 entries, one of which they removed themselves (0c04c01c); Codex confirmed the removal list and the tree diffs before the push; lambdaclass has no notes refs and none were created. ~agent/audit-clone is kept unchanged as evidence with LEAK-EVIDENCE-README.txt

column4: CI run 42424028055 (train legacydocs at 4d0355a56e, a docs-only change over 93850111) failed Kernel replay (leanchecker): the per-module leg replayed ConcreteSpec.Spec.Ownership, a module renamed to Slice1Ownership by 44ee1231, and stopped on unknown constant 'ConcreteSpec.lookupF'. The job's lake cache had been restored through a restore-key prefix from the cache of train commit 5b894432ad, whose sources predate the rename. Non-fresh `leanchecker ConcreteSpec` picks every .olean on the search path whose name has the prefix (the toolchain's LeanChecker.lean, lines 91-94), so orphaned build files are replayed. Reproducer: build 44ee1231^, build 93850111's sources over that build directory, run scripts/proofs/kernel_replay.sh: FAIL on the Checker/Syntax orphans; a clean build of the same sources passes. Codex confirmed it with that reproducer (2026-11-07). Structural cause: the replay took its module list from the build directory's contents instead of the sources.
column7: closed by wip/replay-source-modules: kernel_replay.sh replays a staged library holding exactly the modules the sources declare and checks that the replayed set equals that list; scripts/proofs/lib.sh prunes build files of modules with no source before building; negative controls plant an orphan that fails an unfiltered replay and is ignored by the staged one

column4: Slice 0's backend stages are superlinear (found by the scaling gate on wip/gate-scaling-determinism 4ed5b4e1; confirmed by Codex from source, 2026-11-08). Measured on fede-256gb with `lake env lean --run` over a WF BIR family scaled k (2k+1 blocks, 4 instructions per body block), minimum of 3 interleaved runs, emit forced by a linear structural digest: LCB.emit 0.18 ms / 27.9 ms / 21584 ms at k = 1 / 10 / 100 (10x->100x exponent 2.89); LLVM.module 0.11 / 0.49 / 16.1 ms (1.52); LCB.assemble 0.60 / 4.46 / 52.5 ms (1.07). Reproducer: scripts/checks/compiler/scaling.lean (measure 1 3 x86_64-linux) with the reprStr digest replaced by a structural one. Cause: Concrete/Backend/LCB.lean regId (line 103) rebuilds ids p (lines 75-79, a blockBase/instBase prefix sum per entry, Theta(k^2)) on every operand lookup, so adapt is Theta(k^3); numberingOk (95-99) adds quadratic Nodup and membership checks; adaptPhi scans all blocks per phi. Concrete/Backend/LLVM.lean print (87-90) calls phis (64-69), which rebuilds and filters edges p (57-62) per block, Theta(k^2). Structural cause: closed specification functions (the numbering and predecessor relations as functions of position, chosen for the proofs) also serve directly as executable queries, with no prepared table. A performance defect, not a semantic one: results are unchanged.
column7: LCB.emit and LLVM.module build the numbering and the incoming-edge table once (running offsets; a lookup map; linear validation), proved equal to the reference definitions so adapter_correct and emit_correct keep their exact statements, and the scaling gate measures every in-process stage at a 10x->100x exponent of at most 1.35 on concrete-ci-2
